scenario: LTHE.2.5.3 — the case both readings of `latest` agree on, pinned so a fix for the other vectors cannot lose it. DoorOpen at ts 1, DoorOpen at ts 2, Motion at ts 3, one pump. The ts-2 DoorOpen precedes the Motion and matches it, so it excludes the ts-1 anchor: the rule fires exactly once, logging `2`. Without `latest` it would fire twice. The log reads the anchor's `n`, which mirrors its `ts`, because `ts` is a `Time` ([LFAC.9.1]) and the vector should not depend on how a `Time` renders.
rules_ds:
schema DoorOpen scope ttl 1_h:
    loc: String
    n: Int
    ts: Time

schema Motion scope ttl 1_h:
    loc: String
    ts: Time

rule entry:
    latest DoorOpen d
    then Motion within 30_s
->
    log info "{d.n}"
